findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes and placed in their own tasks
findings.description: Every commit point is written as `- [ ] **Commit:** ...` inside its own "Task N.x: Commit" (lines 93-96, 176-179, 246-249, 283-286, 322-325). Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes. Five standalone commit tasks, each with a `git add` checkbox, are also too granular. Fix: delete Tasks 1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3 and 5.5. Put a plain `**Commit**: feat: ...` line at the end of the last tested task in each section (after 1.4, 2.3, 3.5, 4.2 and 5.4).

findings.title: Section 4 commits config changes without running the tests that load those files
findings.description: Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 change `config/default.yaml` and `config/test.yaml`, and check them only with a `python -c` print. Task 4.3 then commits. The full suite doesn't run until Task 5.1, which has no commit after it for any fixes. At least two tests load the shipped configs directly: `tests/test_config.py:45` (`test_default_config_file_loads`) and `tests/test_main.py:70`, which starts the server with `default.yaml`. Changing the default policy to `wrap` changes runtime behavior there, so the commit doesn't sit at a tested point. Fix: run `pytest` at the end of Task 4.2, before the Section 4 commit marker. Task 5.1 can then go, because Task 5.2 step 2 already runs the suite.

findings.title: The WRAP plan states a `[0, width)` guarantee that `np.mod` alone doesn't give
findings.description:
SC7 requires every wrapped position to land in the half-open range `[0, width) × [0, height)`. Task 2.2 says to use only `np.mod(..., out=...)` and claims it produces values in `[0, width)`. The Notes at line 330 repeat the claim. With floats, a tiny negative overshoot rounds up to the top of the range: `np.mod(-1e-17, 100.0)` returns `100.0`. So SC7 can be broken. The integration assertion `0 <= x < width` in Task 3.4 would then fail rarely and unpredictably. None of the Task 2.3 tests hit this case.

Fix:
- Add a step to Task 2.2 that maps results equal to `width`/`height` to `0.0`, for example `positions[:, 0][positions[:, 0] >= width] = 0.0`.
- Add a test in Task 2.3, such as `test_wrap_tiny_negative_overshoot`, where position `(-1e-17, 50)` must give `x < 100`.
- Correct the Note at line 330.

findings.title: The round-trip test checks only the policy, not the whole config SC5 asks for
findings.description: SC5 says "reloading the emitted YAML produces an equal `ServerConfig`." Task 1.4's `test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip` asserts only that the policy matches. Fix: change the assertion to `reloaded == original`, using frozen dataclass equality. That also catches the enum being written out as a Python repr, which is the risk the slice design names at lines 224-227.

findings.title: Line references are stale
findings.description: Task 1.1 places `WorldBoundsConfig` at line 25, but it is at `src/migratory_server/config.py:47`. Task 1.3 places `_validate_world_bounds` "around line 156", but it is at `config.py:180`. The symbol names are enough for an implementer. Drop the line numbers or treat them as approximate.

findings.title: Task 3.2's "zero import-time overhead" step contradicts the Notes
findings.description: Task 3.2 asks the implementer to "Confirm the `OPEN` path has zero import-time ... overhead." Task 3.2's own first step imports `apply_bounds_policy` at module level, and the Notes (line 329) say the import is not avoided. Nobody can confirm that step as written. The mock test in Task 3.4 already covers SC10. Reword the step to "no per-tick call when policy is `OPEN`", or drop it.

findings.title: Task 2.3 has some redundant tests
findings.description: The parametrized "dispatches correctly and does not raise" test repeats what the per-policy tests above it already check. You could also merge `test_open_is_noop_positions` and `test_open_is_noop_velocities`. Otherwise the test list fits the slice's explicit "full unit test coverage" scope.

findings.title: No load-test task is needed
findings.description: The slice has no NFR section. Its only performance statement is that the `OPEN` path costs a negligible amount, and SC10 checks that with a mock test. No NFR is left uncovered, so a `tests/load/` task and CI wiring aren't required for this slice.
